items.title: Rapper Balendra Shah sworn in as Nepal's youngest PM

featured_image.name: Shah sworn in as Nepal's prime minister -Xinhua

items.description:
Balendra Shah, a 35-year-old rapper-turned-politician popularly known as "Balen," was sworn in as Nepal's prime minister on Friday, becoming the youngest leader in the country's democratic history and the first from the Madhesi community of the southern plains to hold the office. President Ram Chandra Paudel administered the oath at the presidential residence in Kathmandu.[1][2][3]

Shah wore skin-tight trousers, a matching jacket, his signature black Nepali cloth cap, and sunglasses to the ceremony, according to Reuters. On the eve of his swearing-in, he posted a new music video on Facebook stressing patriotism: "Nepal is not scared this time, the heart is full of red blood ... laughter and happiness will reach every household this time," he sang.[1]

items.title: Trump presses Saudi Arabia on Abraham Accords at Miami summit

featured_image.name: Trump Presses Saudis to Recognize Israel as He Defends Iran ...

items.description: President Donald Trump delivered the closing address Friday at the Saudi-backed Future Investment Initiative summit in Miami Beach, using the platform to once again press Saudi Arabia to normalize relations with Israel by joining the Abraham Accords — a call he has made repeatedly since his 2025 visit to Riyadh, where he described the prospect as his "dream".[1][2]

items.title: MIT's VibeGen AI designs proteins by how they move

featured_image.name: MIT engineers design proteins by their motion, not just ...

items.description: MIT engineers have developed an AI model called VibeGen that designs proteins based on how they move rather than how they look, a advance that could reshape drug development, materials science, and synthetic biology. The work, published March 24 in the journal Matter, represents the first time scientists can specify a target pattern of motion and have an AI system generate a protein sequence to match it.[1]

items.title: Iranian strike injures 10 US troops at Saudi base

featured_image.name: U.S. military refueling plane crashes in Iraq | PBS News

items.description:
An Iranian missile and drone attack struck Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia on Friday, injuring 10 American service members and damaging multiple U.S. refueling aircraft, according to The Wall Street Journal, citing U.S. and Arab officials. Two of the wounded troops sustained serious injuries, the officials said.[1][2]

The injured personnel were inside a building on the base when it was hit. At least one missile and several drones struck the facility, which serves as a logistics and operational hub for U.S. forces in the region.[1]

items.title: Iran agrees to let humanitarian aid pass through Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Strait of Hormuz: Which countries’ ships has Iran allowed safe passage to?

items.description:
Iran announced on Friday that it will "facilitate and expedite" the safe passage of humanitarian aid and agricultural shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first breakthrough at the contested waterway since war erupted nearly a month ago.

Ali Bahreini, Iran's ambassador to the United Nations in Geneva, said Tehran had accepted a formal request from the UN to allow the shipments through the critical strait, which normally handles a fifth of the world's oil traffic and nearly a third of global fertilizer trade. "This measure reflects Iran's continued commitment to supporting humanitarian efforts and ensuring that essential aid reaches those in need without delay," Bahreini said in a post on X. He added that operational arrangements would be finalized with the United Nations "at the appropriate time".[1][2][3]

items.title: Israel strikes Iran's nuclear sites as war nears one month

featured_image.name: Israel strikes Tehran on Persian New Year | AP News

items.description: Israel launched a new wave of strikes on Iran early Friday, targeting weapons production facilities and nuclear infrastructure as diplomatic efforts to end the nearly month-old war remained deadlocked, with Washington and Tehran exchanging competing ceasefire proposals through intermediaries.

items.title: China protests after scholar's suicide tied to US interrogation

featured_image.name: The heartbreaking death of a Chinese postdoctoral scholar, who took own  life after being subjected to hostile questioning by U.S. law enforcement  personnel, calls into question once again the impact and legitimacy

items.description:
China's Foreign Ministry on Friday called on the United States to conduct a thorough investigation into the death of a Chinese postdoctoral researcher who took his own life a day after being interrogated by U.S. law enforcement personnel, escalating a diplomatic dispute over Washington's treatment of Chinese academics on American soil.

Spokesperson Lin Jian, speaking at a regular press briefing in Beijing, said China was "deeply saddened by the heartbreaking death" and had formally lodged a protest with Washington. Chinese diplomatic missions had "swiftly got in touch with the researcher's family and actively assisted them in handling relevant matters," Lin said.[1][2]

items.title: Trump signals to allies no imminent Iran ground invasion

featured_image.name: US Signals No Immediate Plans for Iran Ground Invasion to ...

items.description: The Trump administration is telling allies it has no immediate plans for a ground invasion of Iran, even as the Pentagon weighs sending up to 10,000 additional troops to the Middle East and lawmakers scramble to impose limits on a conflict now entering its second month.

items.title: Hezbollah confirms more than 400 fighters killed as Israel conflict grows

featured_image.name: More than 400 Hezbollah fighters killed in new war with ...

items.description: More than 400 Hezbollah fighters have been killed since the Lebanese armed group launched its opening salvoes against Israel on March 2, according to two sources familiar with Hezbollah's internal count who spoke to Reuters. The figure represents the first comprehensive tally of the group's combat losses in a conflict now entering its fourth week, as Israel continues both aerial bombardments and an expanding ground offensive across southern Lebanon.[1]

items.title: IRGC claims destruction of US refueling fleet at Al-Kharj base

featured_image.name: Satellite images show more aircraft at Saudi airbase used by ...

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced on Friday the launch of the 84th wave of Operation True Promise 4, claiming to have destroyed U.S. aerial refueling vehicles and logistical support aircraft at the Al-Kharj base in Saudi Arabia, home to Prince Sultan Air Base. The IRGC described the strike as a "special joint missile and drone operation" carried out by its Aerospace Force with assistance from the IRGC Navy.[1][2]

The operation marks the latest in a relentless campaign of Iranian strikes against U.S. and Israeli military assets across the Middle East, now approaching its first month since the war began on February 28.

items.title: Houthis outline red lines for joining Iran war

featured_image.name: US sinks Houthi boats in the Red Sea: How did the fight unfold?

items.description: Yemen's Houthi rebels on Friday issued their most explicit warning yet that they are prepared to enter the ongoing US-Israeli war against Iran, with military spokesperson Yahya Saree outlining three conditions under which the group would take direct action. The declaration raises the prospect of a second major maritime chokepoint closure that analysts warn could compound an already severe global energy crisis.

items.title: China and Pakistan agree to jointly push for ceasefire in Iran war

featured_image.name: Australia Invites China Foreign Minister Wang Yi to Visit Late March: SCMP  - Bloomberg

items.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi voiced support on Friday for Pakistan's efforts to mediate between the United States and Iran, calling peace talks essential to preventing further casualties and restoring safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz, as diplomatic channels showed fragile signs of movement amid a nearly month-long war.

items.title: UN creates task force to protect Hormuz trade as Iran tightens grip on strait

featured_image.name: Shipping slows to a crawl through Strait of Hormuz ...

items.description:
The United Nations on Friday announced the creation of a task force to safeguard humanitarian trade through the Strait of Hormuz, even as Iran moved to tighten its grip on the waterway by pursuing legislation to codify transit fees and turning back ships attempting passage.

UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres ordered the task force to develop mechanisms for keeping fertilizer and agricultural products flowing through the strait, which has been effectively closed since the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran began on February 28. "The prolonged closure of the Strait is choking the movement of oil, gas and fertiliser at a critical moment in the global planting season," Guterres said. The task force, led by Jorge Moreira da Silva of the UN Office for Project Services, will include representatives from the International Maritime Organization and the International Chamber of Commerce, and draws on the model of the Black Sea Grain Initiative.[1][2]

items.title: Israel hits Iran nuclear sites, steel plants as IRGC closes Hormuz

featured_image.name: Iran says nuclear facilities hit by strikes after Israel warns attacks  'will escalate'

items.description: Israel launched a fresh wave of strikes against Iran on Friday, hitting two nuclear facilities and two of the country's largest steel plants, as Iran's Revolutionary Guards declared the Strait of Hormuz closed and warned that any vessel attempting to pass would face "harsh measures." The escalation came even as U.S. officials signaled they expect the nearly month-old conflict to wind down within weeks.

items.title: Iran strikes Israel, Gulf states as IRGC warns civilians to flee US bases

featured_image.name: Iran sends waves of missiles into Israel, dismisses Trump's talk of  negotiations as 'fake news' - The Sen Times

items.description: Iran launched fresh waves of ballistic missiles and drones at Israel and multiple Gulf Arab nations on Friday, the 28th day of the war that began when the United States and Israel struck Iran on February 28. As air raid sirens sounded across Israel and Gulf capitals scrambled air defenses, Israel's Defense Minister Israel Katz warned that Israeli strikes on Iran would "escalate and expand," while Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps issued an ominous call for civilians across the region to evacuate areas near American forces.

items.title: Iran death toll tops 1,900 as IFRC warns of deepening crisis

featured_image.name: UN says nearly 22,000 civilian buildings in Iran damaged - Yahoo

items.description:
More than 1,900 people have been killed and at least 20,000 injured in Iran since the United States and Israel launched coordinated strikes on February 28, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said on Friday. Maria Martinez of the IFRC, citing figures from the Iranian Red Crescent, said the organization remains the only major humanitarian body operating nationwide amid the escalating conflict.[1][2]

The death toll, which has climbed steadily over the past four weeks, marks a sharp increase from earlier estimates. By mid-March, Iranian authorities had reported roughly 1,444 deaths. The IFRC cautioned that relief efforts are continuing under severe shortages and ongoing security threats.[3][2][4][5]

items.title: Witkoff says he expects Iran talks 'this week' on 15-point peace plan

featured_image.name: U.S. envoy Witkoff says Iran is seeking an off-ramp | Reuters

items.description:
U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff said Friday he expects meetings with Iran "this week" to end the month-long war in the Middle East, expressing optimism that Washington's peace framework could bring Tehran to the table. "We think there will be meetings this week, we're certainly hopeful for it," Witkoff told the Saudi-backed Future Investment Initiative summit in Miami, according to AFP. "We have a 15-point plan on the table. We expect the Iranians to respond. It could solve it all."[1]

The remarks come a day after Witkoff confirmed during a White House Cabinet meeting that the 15-point proposal had been delivered to Iran through Pakistan, which is serving as the primary intermediary. Pakistan's role as a diplomatic bridge between Washington and Tehran has become central to the nascent peace effort, even as Iran publicly rejects the American plan and fighting continues across the region.[2][3]

items.title: IRGC confirms Strait of Hormuz closure as strikes hit Iran's steel, nuclear sites

featured_image.name: Iran war live: Tehran vows retaliation for Israeli hits on nuclear sites

items.description: American and Israeli warplanes struck two of Iran's largest steel production facilities and key nuclear sites on Friday, escalating a nearly month-old military campaign as Tehran vowed retaliation that would go "beyond eye for an eye" and released a list of steel plants across the Middle East it intends to target.

items.title: Iran accuses US-Israel of genocide at UN Human Rights Council

featured_image.name: Iran Foreign Minister to Address UN Human Rights Council

items.description:
Iran has made at least 20 formal communications to the International Criminal Court documenting what it calls intentional violations of international humanitarian law in the ongoing US-Israeli military campaign, the vice-president of the Iranian Red Crescent Society confirmed this week.[1][2]

Razieh Alishvandi, the deputy head of the Iranian Red Crescent Society for international and human rights affairs, said Iran has also contacted the World Health Organization and the International Committee of the Red Cross to report the scale of civilian casualties and destruction across the country. Five joint statements by the Iranian National Committee on Humanitarian Law and the Red Crescent Society have been issued documenting attacks on medical centers, ambulances, and civilians, according to Iranian state media outlet Press TV.[2][1]

items.title: US can confirm only a third of Iran's missiles destroyed

featured_image.name: US can only confirm about a third of Iran's missile arsenal ...

items.description: Nearly a month into the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, American intelligence assessments show the United States can only confirm the destruction of roughly one-third of Iran's vast missile arsenal, according to a Reuters exclusive citing five people familiar with the intelligence. The finding undercuts President Donald Trump's assertion at a Cabinet meeting on Thursday that Iran has "very few rockets left".[1][2][3]
